title: Gilbert and Varshamov Meet Johnson: List-Decoding Explicit Nearly-Optimal Binary Codes
authors: Silas Richelson (University of California, USA), Sourya Roy (University of California, USA)
abstract: We give an efficient algorithm for list-decoding the binary code by Ta-Shma (STOC 2017) to the Johnson Bound. Ta-Shma's code has distance $\frac{1-\ep}{2}$ and rate $\Omega\bigl(\ep^{2+o(1)}\bigr)$ and thus it almost achieves the Gilbert-Varshamov bound. Johnson bound states that such codes are combinatorially list decodable upto $\frac{1-\rho}{2}-$ fraction of errors as long as $\rho\geq\sqrt{\ep}$. We give a polynomial time decoding algorithm that nearly achieves this bound. Thus our result implies the only known binary code that simultaneously nearly achieves both the Gilbert-Varshamov and the Johnson bounds. Our decoding algorithm is based on semi-definite programming hierarchies and includes a new rounding step which might be of independent interest.

algorithms in [10], [11] comes via a new method for

algorithm. We explain this in detail next in Section I-C. However, before getting into the technical

via Expander RWs

parity samplers for “good” pseudodistributions. For
a pseudodistribution to be “good”, it must satisfy
the technical requirements speciﬁed below. We will
show later on that if O is the pseudodistribution
obtained by solving the SDP of the decoding algorithm, then the pseudodistribution O(S,σ) will
be good with non-negligible probability over the
slice (S, σ). This will require adopting the argument
of [15] to our modiﬁed rounding technique. We
handle this, and other issues in Section II-D. For the
remainder of this section, we ﬁx a good pseudodistribution O on {0, 1}A , where A is a λ−expander.
